summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 69 of CipherBox (porting the node/v3 model + grant-root awareness to the Rust FUSE/WinFsp desktop stack) end-to-end via the GSD workflow, auto-advancing from planning into execution.
summary.outcome: Planning completed (18 plans across 7+ waves after two re-scopes); execution merged 13/18 plans (the entire crates/core + crates/sdk read/rotation/seal/emit/write-owner-materialization foundation, all green). The final atomic FUSE consumer flip (69-09) proved to be a >1000-site, unverifiable-by-compile crypto migration; after three successive architectural blockers and re-scopes, the user approved a chunked multi-session 'grind' gated on a live e2e run, and a runbook was being written/committed when the transcript ends — 69-09, 69-10, 69-13 remain unmerged and 69-14 (WinFsp) is deferred to the user's Windows machine.

repo: node/v3 crate split: crates/core owns Node enum/codec/AAD-seal (pure), crates/sdk owns listing/rotation/floor_store (stateful), crates/fuse is the FUSE/WinFsp adapter.
D-04 mandates a clean flag-day cutover (no dual legacy/node-v3 model) since there are no production vaults yet — greenfield migration.
D-07 dual-keying: read plane keyed by SealedChildRef.ipnsName, write plane keyed by WriteChildRef.childId (UUID); must never pair the two by ipnsName.
Terminal-owner zeroization rule: parent_read_key/parent_write_key are passed by borrow (&[u8]) so the type system prevents zeroing caller-owned buffers; only self-minted keys get zeroed.

InodeKind in crates/fuse is a full read-WRITE vault-owner state (holds ipns_private_key + folder_key/file_key to sign IPNS records and seal new children) — not a read-only client like the TS web 68.2 mirror.

ResolvedChild (crates/sdk/src/listing.rs) intentionally carries no key material; resolve_child unseals the child read-key and immediately zeroizes it — a separate write-owner materialization API (69-17's ResolvedOwnedChild) was needed to recover read_key+write_key+ipns_private_key together.

crates/sdk/src/queue.rs JournalOp originally used hex-string fields for user-ECIES-under-self.public_key wrapping — completely different crypto model from node/v3's symmetric parent-key sealing; reshaping it (69-18) is a separate concern from the fuse consumer flip.

Feature-gate linchpin: crates/fuse/Cargo.toml default=["fuse"]; platform/windows/* is behind #[cfg(feature="winfsp")] and excluded from default `cargo check --workspace` (only verified under `--features winfsp` in cargo-windows CI).

Project memory confirms crypto migrations that pass `cargo check`/mocked tests have shipped runtime-broken before (48/89 E2E broke on a zeroization change, a D-07 conflation shipped compile-clean) — compile-green is not sufficient proof for this class of change; needs live sdk-e2e/desktop-e2e with docker+TEE.
GSD gsd commit helper has a recurring false-negative: reports commit_failed while the commit actually lands cleanly — must always verify via `git log --oneline -1`, never blindly retry.

code.finding: InodeKind::{Folder,File} store folder_key/ipns_private_key/file_ipns_private_key — a read-write owner shape, not just a read cache; comment notes it's 'Critical for write operations.'
ResolvedChild carries only {ipns_name, name, kind, size, modified_at, sequence} — no key material; resolve_child (~line 307-315) unseals the child read-key then zeroizes it immediately.

The originally-cited 'JournalOp.parent_metadata: FolderMetadata cross-crate weld' does not exist in the live tree — JournalOp::{UploadFile,MkdirPublish} only ever had hex-string ECIES fields (wrapped_key_hex, parent_ipns_key_hex, etc.); this stale research claim caused a wasted P1b attempt.
build_child_refs mints SealedChildRef (by ipnsName) and WriteChildRef (by childId UUID) — the D-07 dual-keying entrypoint that 69-17/69-18/69-09 all depend on.

workflow: For a large parallel wave-based execution plan, dispatch the first plan synchronously as a canary to validate the executor→worktree→merge→build pipeline before fanning out later waves in parallel.

When a plan is scoped 'sdk-green but workspace-red by design' (e.g. 69-18 reshaping a type consumed elsewhere), do not merge it alone — continue the dependent plan on the same branch and merge both as one combined workspace-green unit.

To resume a crashed/stalled worktree executor without losing progress, dispatch a fresh executor instructed to operate inside the existing worktree via `git -C`/absolute paths and continue committing on the existing branch, rather than restarting from the dispatch base.

Distinguish a session/usage-limit death from an architectural blocker by checking whether the worktree has any actual edits/commits — zero edits after a stall/limit means it's safe to just re-dispatch once capacity resets.

Recovering from a mid-run planner crash: spawn a fresh single-plan-mode planner to write just the missing plan rather than restarting the whole planning run; then explicitly check/fix requirements frontmatter gaps (e.g. TEST-03 missing from any plan's requirements: field).
Maintain a durable scratchpad handoff file across long unattended executions/pauses so state survives context compaction or ScheduleWakeup resumes.
When two plans in the same wave touch the same file (e.g. crates/sdk/src/lib.rs), run them serialized rather than in parallel even though the wave grouping nominally allows concurrency.

friction: gsd-planner crashed mid-run via an API connection error while writing the phase's plans, requiring filesystem-fallback recovery (13/14 plans landed, had to detect and backfill the missing one).
69-16 executor stalled mid-stream on an API error, leaving uncommitted work that had to be manually inspected, completed, and committed by the orchestrator.
First 69-09 (P1b) execution attempt died from an account session/usage limit reset, not a real blocker, wasting a dispatch cycle.
The gsd commit helper repeatedly false-negatived 'commit_failed' even when commits landed, requiring manual git log verification after every commit.

Executors repeatedly mis-reported their worktree's `expected_base` as their own last docs commit rather than the true fork base, requiring manual `git merge-base` verification before every merge to avoid a bad merge.

Three successive, deeper architectural blockers were discovered only during execution (read/write path not separable → write-plane emit API missing → write-owner tree-materialization API missing → JournalOp still on legacy hex-ECIES model), each requiring a fresh research+planning re-scope cycle instead of being caught during initial planning.

The final atomic FUSE consumer flip (69-09) turned out to be a >1000-site, ~12,300 LOC crypto-model rewrite with no compiling intermediate state, unverifiable by `cargo check` alone — two dedicated executor attempts halted rather than risk shipping unverified crypto changes.
Working directory drifted mid-session, causing a bash command to fail until absolute paths were used.
open_items: 69-09 (atomic Unix FUSE flip onto node/v3) is mid-grind per a newly written 69-09-GRIND-RUNBOOK.md — chunked into bounded per-session slices, RED intermediate commits accepted, final merge gated on a real local sdk-e2e + desktop-e2e run rather than compile-green.
69-10 (delete legacy crates/core types) and 69-13 (grant-gated write path + SC#2 + D-07) remain unexecuted, waiting on 69-09.
69-14 (WinFsp/Windows integration, TEST-03) is explicitly deferred to the user's Windows machine (autonomous: false).
Plan-checker flagged that the SC#6 CI grep-gate (69-06/69-09) uses a placeholder symbol name that must be swapped for the real crate-private resolve symbol at execution time.
VALIDATION.md frontmatter draft-status warning from the plan-checker was fixed, but the SC#6 CI gate wiring itself still needs final confirmation once 69-09 lands.
